```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r include=FALSE}
require(tidyverse)
require(tigerstats)
davisdata <- read.csv(file="UCDavis.csv")
data=davisdata
```
 Our Goal is to answer this question Is there a difference between the alcohol consumed between the row
 you choose to sit in??

# introduction
the question is this; is there a relationship between where you sit in class and how much you drink?   
data from UCDavis math 116 class   
$H_O$ there is no relationship between what row in class you sit and how much you drink.  
$H_A$ there is a difference between what row you sit in class and how much you drink.  


# Methods  
seat is categorical   
alcohol is numerical  


# data summaries



## Now add in boxplot

```{r}
boxplot(alcohol~Seat,data=davisdata)
```

Graph demonstrates that if the students sits in the back they are more ounces per week of alcohol than the students who sit in the front or middle. 





## Numerical Summaries

```{r}
favstats(alcohol~Seat,data=davisdata)
```

The numerical summary shows that the students who sit in the back drink about ten more ounces of alcohol than the students who sit in the front and middle seats who drink about 2 to 3 ounces of alcohol per week.


## Inferential Tests

```{r}
model1 <- aov(alcohol~Seat,data=davisdata)
summary.aov(model1)
```

The p value is 0.000116 which is less than 0.05 so we fail to reject the $H_0$ and conclude that there is a relationship between where someone sits and how much they drink.

```{r}
plot(TukeyHSD(model1))
```

The tukey graph shows there is a difference in alcohol consumption between students who sit in the front and back and middle and back. there is no difference in alcohol consumption between the front and middle rows.
